correctness.summary: Normalization reduces the problem to minimizing the sup norm of (1-u x)(1-v x) on [a,1] with u,v in [0,2]. The unconstrained Chebyshev solution is feasible exactly for kappa<=1+sqrt(2). In the complementary branch an endpoint lower bound is attained uniquely, up to order, by u=2 and v=2/(1+2a); its interior extremum remains below the endpoint level exactly in the stated regime. The general m-stage lower bound follows at lambda=mu, and deterministic checks reproduce the formulas and comparison identities.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Classical sources establish unrestricted Chebyshev semi-iteration and discuss instability of individual factorized stages; related stationary second-degree, learned finite-step, and restricted-zero minimax problems were also checked. No checked source stated the exact interval-uniform two-stage minimax frontier under factorwise Euclidean nonexpansiveness, its kappa=1+sqrt(2) transition, the unique boundary pair, or the all-m no-Chebyshev-order barrier. Full theorem-level text of the 1961 Golub-Varga papers was not inspected and remains the principal residual coverage risk.

value.summary: The result gives a sharp quantitative tradeoff between factorwise stability and Chebyshev acceleration: safe variation strictly improves repeated optimal Richardson at two stages, but beyond a precise condition-number threshold it cannot match unrestricted Chebyshev, and enforcing the same safety at every stage loses square-root condition-number acceleration.

limitations: Exact arithmetic and symmetric positive-definite matrices only.
The criterion is uniform over a continuous spectral interval; a finite known spectrum may permit better tailored parameters.
Euclidean factorwise nonexpansiveness is a strong stability requirement and is not asserted to be necessary for floating-point stability.
Stable three-term Chebyshev recurrences and parameter orderings that allow temporary amplification are outside the imposed constraint.
No floating-point backward-stability or implementation-performance claim is made.
Nonsymmetric, indefinite, nonlinear, stochastic, adaptive, momentum, conjugate-gradient, and line-search methods are outside the claim.
Full theorem-level text of the 1961 Golub-Varga papers was not inspected, leaving residual originality risk.
Independent audit has not been performed.
